final_candidates.decision_summary: Lys119 forms the indispensable Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutating it to alanine directly abolishes catalytic PLP binding and enzyme activity.
G307S is the canonical B6-nonresponsive homocystinuria mutation, severely inactivating catalytic activity while retaining overall fold.
Arginine substitution at position 119 prevents covalent aldimine linkage with PLP, functionally inactivating CBS catalytic turnover.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is fully converged on high-confidence catalytic null substitutions.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the essential Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; substitution with Ala completely abrogates PLP binding and catalytic activity.
Lys119 forms the essential Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutating it to alanine directly abolishes catalytic PLP binding and enzyme function.
I278T is the most prevalent homocystinuria mutation in CBS, causing severe misfolding of the catalytic domain and profound loss of enzymatic activity.
I278T is a well-established severe loss-of-function mutation, though it ranks below active-site nulls due to partial responsiveness to chemical chaperones.
G307S is a classic pathogenic homocystinuria mutation that disrupts the catalytic core geometry and abolishes enzymatic function.
G307S is the canonical B6-nonresponsive homocystinuria mutation, causing severe catalytic inactivation without complete protein degradation.
T191M is a well-characterized severe homocystinuria mutation in the catalytic pocket that results in complete loss of CBS activity.
T191M is a pathogenic mutation causing misfolding and reduced activity, but is less direct than cofactor-binding disruption.
Replacing the catalytic lysine with arginine preserves charge but eliminates the primary amine required for PLP Schiff base formation.
Arginine at position 119 cannot form the requisite covalent aldimine linkage with PLP, functionally abolishing CBS catalytic activity.
Cys52 serves as an axial ligand for heme coordination; substitution to Arg disrupts heme binding and severely destabilizes active enzyme formation.
Cys52 serves as an axial ligand to the regulatory heme; disrupting it impairs stability and activity but may leave basal activity intact.
His65 acts as the second axial ligand coordinating the heme iron; mutating it impairs cofactor integration and CBS activity.
Disrupts the His65 heme axial coordination, lowering enzyme efficiency through regulatory/structural impairment.
P49L is a clinically documented loss-of-function homocystinuria mutation in the heme-binding domain that markedly impairs enzyme activity.
Located in the N-terminal heme-binding region, causing structural perturbation but with less guaranteed complete loss of function.
